exposure: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) status (based on bile acid levels: normal, mild, moderate-severe, not obtained)
cohort: The study included singleton pregnancies diagnosed with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) between 1 May 2014 and 31 December 2017.
finding: The study found that specific AST (27.5 IU/L) and ALT (26.7 IU/L) levels predicted elevated bile acids, but there were no significant differences in most obstetric interventions or neonatal outcomes among women with normal, mild, or moderate-severe ICP, suggesting that ICP should not be presumed based solely on pruritus to avoid complications from early term delivery.
mod_finding: The rate of labor inductions was high across all groups of women, irrespective of their bile acid levels.
